patent_summary: The document discloses a two-step preparation of tembotrione in which methyl 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate is etherified with sodium trifluoroethoxide in the presence of MOH or M2CO3 (M = Li, Na or K) to give 2-chloro-3-(trifluoroethoxymethyl)-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid, which is then condensed with 1,3-cyclohexanedione in a reaction solvent under a condensing agent (CDI, HBTU, HOBT or DBU) and a base catalyst (sodium carbonate, potassium carbonate, calcium hydroxide, triethylamine or pyridine) to give the product. Dependent claims specify the molar ratios, solvent choices, solvent-to-substrate weight ratio and the temperature and time windows for each of the two steps.
novelty_claims: The patent positions its advance as the choice of reagent in step a: claim 1 requires "methyl 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-(methanesulfonyl)benzoate and sodium trifluoroethoxide as the reaction substrates", the preformed alkoxide replacing the trifluoroethanol plus potassium tert-butoxide combination that the abstract objects to as giving "low yield" with an "expensive" potassium tert-butoxide reagent. Against the second prior-art route it cites, in which the carboxyl group is converted to the acid chloride and then to an ester before rearrangement, the abstract's stated advantage is that this process needs no acetone cyanohydrin, which it describes as a highly toxic catalyst. On that basis it asserts high yield, low cost, ease of operation, little pollution and safety, and suitability for large-scale industrial production. These are the document's own assertions: the example yields it prints are claims read off the page and are not verified here, and nine of the eighteen annotated reaction steps carry a molar_mass_inconsistent flag and five a mass_balance_implausible flag, so nothing in this annotation confirms them. Examples 1 to 5 are five alternative runs of the same two-step route, differing in base, condensing agent, solvent and temperature, not a longer sequence.
